subject: Urgent: Atlas Retail latency/errors — dedicated pool headroom squeeze
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@atlas-retail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in latency and 5xxs for Atlas Retail production (region us-west)

Mina,

We started seeing a sharp spike in end-user latency and intermittent 5xx errors around 07:45 PT this morning for our ingestion pipeline that calls your dedicated endpoint (model: rwd-llm-3-large). 90s+ tail latencies and about 2.3% 5xxs across the last 20 minutes. Throughput has dropped by roughly 30% despite request volumes holding steady. This is impacting checkout flows in several stores.

We need immediate help — can your team confirm whether this is on your side or an application regression? If it’s capacity-related, we need a mitigation plan and an ETA.

Attached are a short sample of error traces.

Thanks,
Samir
VP Engineering, Atlas Retail
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:18:27 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Spike in latency and 5xxs for Atlas Retail production (region us-west)

Team — forwarding Atlas Retail. They report tail latency and 5xx increases on their reserved/dedicated pool (rwd-llm-3-large). Priority: high.

Quick context: Atlas is on a committed reserved capacity plan (deal ATL-2027-Q2-42) with a 95% uptime SLA and reserved throughput guarantees. They’re reporting errors + throughput falloff; early signs point to dedicated GPU pool headroom being thin today (high queue depth).

Ask: Rishi — can you confirm pool headroom and immediate mitigations (burst to spare capacity, cross-region failover, model variant fallback)?
Laura — I'll need a suggested customer message and your recommendation on whether to pre-authorize a credit.
Priyom — FYI and please advise if this needs executive escalation.

Attaching their trace sample from Samir.

— Mina

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:32:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in latency and 5xxs for Atlas Retail production (region us-west)

Mina — investigating. Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the serving telemetry:
- Dedicated pool for rwd-llm-3-large (us-west-dedicated-23) is at 92% GPU utilization across nodes and steady queue depth growth on token service.
- KV cache hit-rate for Atlas’s prefix has dropped (cache eviction earlier this morning after a shorter-than-normal TTL sweep).
- Error traces show OOM transient spikes on a subset of nodes and 503s coming from overloaded token scheduler rather than model runtime.

Immediate mitigations I can kick off (need approvals where noted):
1) Burst: Temporarily assign 4 additional GPU slots from shared spare capacity to us-west-dedicated-23 (impact: minor cost delta).
2) Failover: Shift new incoming requests for Atlas to a cold-standby cluster in us-east with cross-region routing (expected added latency ~30ms but low queueing).
3) Model-fallback: Serve Atlas with rwd-llm-3-medium for non-critical endpoints (reduces token CPU and memory).
4) Cache restore: Force prefix cache warm for Atlas to recover hit-rate (fast, no cost).

I’m starting (4) now. For (1) and (2) I need an exec okay to pull reserved spare GPUs or to enable cross-region overflow; for (3) we should confirm product impact with Laura (does reduced quality for certain calls break SLAs?).

Attaching a capacity snapshot: capacity_snapshot_20270409.csv

— Rishi
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:40:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in latency and 5xxs for Atlas Retail production (region us-west)

Thanks Rishi — good, please proceed with cache warm and validate (4).

Recommendation for customer comms (short):
- Acknowledge impact, share what we’ve observed (high GPU utilization and queueing), and immediate actions we’re taking (cache warm, scoped burst, cross-region overflow).
- Provide ETA: we expect to reduce error rate to <0.5% within 30–45 minutes after burst + cache restore.
- Offer: If SLA is breached as a result of this incident we will issue a credit; recommendation to pre-authorize up to 10% invoice credit so we can act quickly.

Priyom — if we need to pull from reserved spare, we should flag this to execs (possible reallocation of reserved capacity). I think a pre-authorized 10% is reasonable; if Engineering needs more headroom we may come back for a larger credit.

I'll draft the customer message if you want me to send it to Samir.

— Laura
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:00:42 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Atlas Retail — request exec decision on temporary reserved reallocation and pre-authorized credit

Vivek / Priyom — Atlas (ATL-2027-Q2-42) is experiencing capacity-driven latency and 5xx spikes in us-west. Rishi's telemetry shows dedicated pool us-west-dedicated-23 at 92% with queue growth and some OOM transients. We are mid-mitigation: cache warm is in progress and we can failover to us-east.

Two asks that require executive sign-off now:
1) Short-term reserved reallocation: allow Engineering to pull 4 reserved GPU slots from the regional spare/reserved buffer for up to 3 hours to stabilize Atlas. This will temporarily reduce spare capacity for other reserved customers by a small margin.
2) Pre-approve up to 10% invoice credit commitment should the SLA be breached while we remediate. Laura recommends this so we can communicate quickly and prevent churn.

Attached: sla_risk_playbook.pdf (quick steps & customer wording).

I propose we tell Atlas:
- We see a capacity pressure event; immediate mitigations are in effect (cache warm, burst to spare, cross-region overflow).
- ETA: error rate to <0.5% within 30–45 minutes.
- We’ll follow up with RCA and remediation plan.

Please advise quickly — Atlas is asking for an ETA and we should not delay the burst if we have approval.

— Mina
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:25:19 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: Atlas Retail — request exec decision on temporary reserved reallocation and pre-authorized credit

Thanks — good triage. Approve the temporary reallocation of 4 GPU slots for up to 3 hours to bring queueing back to normal. Engineering: please proceed and confirm when throughput is back to expected.

On credits: approve pre-authorized communication committing up to a 15% credit cap (higher than Laura’s 10%) if SLA is breached — cap is temporary and will be reconciled after RCA. Finance/legal, please standby for a short memo.

Laura — please send the customer comms (use the draft in sla_risk_playbook.pdf) and offer the credit cap as authorized. Rishi — proceed with failover as needed; give the team a 15-minute status update cadence until stabilized.

— Vivek
